chunks: That which a group informed me of, from Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Hasan — and [also via] Ahmad ibn Ubdun, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr, from Ali ibn al-Hasan — from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him):

He said: I asked, 'May the menstruating woman and the person in a state of janaba recite anything [of the Quran]?' He said: «Yes, whatever they wish, except the prostration verse; and they may remember Allah, exalted be He, in every state.»

His statement, 'they remember Allah, exalted be He, in every state,' indicates what we have [previously] mentioned regarding the permissibility of remembering Allah, exalted be He, while in the state of defecation.

key_terms.السَّجْدَةَ: the prostration verse; a Quranic verse whose recitation makes an immediate prostration (sajda wajiba) obligatory
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: junub; person in a state of major ritual impurity (janaba) due to sexual intercourse or seminal emission
key_terms.الْحَائِضُ: menstruating woman; one in the state of ritual impurity (haid) due to menstrual blood
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: defecation; the state of being in the toilet or in the act of passing stool

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman or a person in a state of janaba recite the Quran, according to Imam al-Baqir in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Transmitted through two parallel chains converging at Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, this hadith records Zurara and/or Muhammad ibn Muslim asking Imam al-Baqir (AS) whether a menstruating woman (ha'id) and a person in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) may recite Quran. The Imam permits it freely except for the obligatory prostration verses (ayat al-sajda), and affirms that both may engage in dhikr in all states. Shaykh al-Tusi appends a juristic inference: the phrase 'in every state' explicitly covers the toilet, establishing the permissibility of dhikr during defecation.
